Topics

What we'll cover

Sessions follow your exam board's specification and your target grade. These are the main areas.

Number and algebra

  • Fractions, percentages and standard form
  • Expressions, equations and formulae
  • Graphs and sequences
  • Quadratics and simultaneous equations

Ratio, proportion and geometry

  • Ratio and proportion
  • Compound measures and rates of change
  • Angles, area and volume
  • Trigonometry and Pythagoras
  • Transformations and vectors (Higher)

Probability and statistics

  • Probability, including tree diagrams
  • Averages and spread
  • Charts and graphs
  • Sampling and cumulative frequency (Higher)

The exams

How the exams work

GCSE Maths is examined in three papers, including a non-calculator paper, at one of two tiers: Foundation (grades 1 to 5) or Higher (grades 4 to 9). Your school decides the tier, and sessions follow it.

Exam technique

Where marks are often lost

  • Not showing working, so method marks are lost even when the answer is wrong
  • Algebra: rearranging formulae and expanding brackets
  • Ratio and proportion problems set in context
  • Unfamiliar multi-step problems where the first step isn't obvious

FAQ

GCSE Maths: common questions

Foundation or Higher tier?

Your school decides which tier a student is entered for. Sessions follow whichever it is. If you're unsure, raise it on the free intro call.

Which exam boards do you teach?

AQA, Edexcel and OCR, among others. Sessions are tailored to the board your school sits.

My child is in Year 7 to 9. Can you help?

Yes, see KS3 Maths & Science, at the same rates as GCSE.
